items.stem: The zeroes of a polynomial x² + px + q are twice the zeroes of the polynomial 4x² − 5x − 6. The value of p is
items.answer: Let α and β be the zeroes of 4x² − 5x − 6, so the zeroes of x² + px + q are 2α and 2β. For 4x² − 5x − 6: α + β = −b/a = −(−5)/4 = 5/4. For x² + px + q: 2α + 2β = −b/a = −p, i.e. 2(α + β) = −p. Substituting α + β = 5/4 gives 2 × 5/4 = −p ⇒ p = −5/2. Thus (a) is the correct option.
